name: Drew Petzing

views.text: An offense should blend old and new football and take its shape from whoever proves best on the roster.
Run the ball well and play-action takes care of itself.
Timing comes from spacing between players, not from where each one lines up.
Copying last year's playbook into a new building is a mistake; fit it to the people there.
Get to know the quarterback as a person first; the football conversations go better after that.
A veteran quarterback wants volume and aggressiveness balanced, and he wants to be coached straight.
When the run stalls, the offense gets predictable, so fixing the run is the first job.
Meetings can be demanding and still be fun; players learn more when they enjoy the room.

signatures: explains a choice as a week-to-week call based on the opponent rather than a fixed rule
sounds the same after a good practice as after a bad one
talks about deception and body language as teaching points for the whole line

motivation.want: to prove his offense can keep a contender's attack among the best
motivation.fear: being remembered as the coordinator who could not follow the success

want.text: to keep Detroit scoring after its last two play-callers left

voice: Calm, technical and even-keeled; he explains concepts like deception, spacing and timing in plain teaching terms and rarely sounds rattled. He is relationship-minded with quarterbacks, upbeat in meetings, and frames scheme decisions as matchups rather than doctrine.

evidence.summary: Gannon names Petzing, 35, the Browns' quarterbacks coach and a former Vikings colleague, as offensive coordinator, saying he picked coaches for thinking and character. No Petzing quotes.

At his introduction he says he studied Murray's tape and called his former coaches and teammates before interviewing, already talks with Murray about personal things more than football, and plans to use Murray's running. Writer calls him relationship-driven.

He describes a blend of traditional and modern football shaped by whichever players prove effective, plans to lean on the run and tight ends while Murray rehabs, and expects Murray under center more. His words via a local outlet.

Under Petzing Murray took about a quarter of his snaps under center in 2023; Petzing's teaching point was selling the run through body language so every look is identical, and he treated alignment as a game-by-game choice. Scheme detail.
Murray relays that Petzing stresses establishing the run, which keeps defenses tight and powers play-action; when the run stalls the offense becomes predictable. Petzing is not quoted.

evidence.publisher: Sports Illustrated (Lions On SI), John Maakaron
evidence.summary: Why Campbell hired him: command of run, protection and pass concepts, attention to detail, a creative Arizona offense with a varied run game and play-action, and a calm, confident, enthusiastic, communicative manner; a former Lions back calls him precise about timing. In the intro video he lists family, food, snowboarding, golf and community work. Campbell's and others' praise; favorable.

OTA feature: Goff praises his communication, energy, accountability and leadership and says meetings are fun; St. Brown is upbeat; Campbell says nothing rattles him, he adapts on the fly, can coach every offensive position and is the same every day. Early reactions before any game.

evidence.publisher: Sports Illustrated (Lions On SI), Vito Chirco
evidence.summary: Piece on the defensive coordinator noting that in OTAs the Lions defense studied Petzing's new looks to prepare for what opponents might show. Indirect, one line about him.
